target.title: fix: reject Telegram topic sessions_send targets
target.body:
Closes #99835

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling `sessions_send` with a Telegram topic session key could dispatch an inter-agent run against the topic child session instead of getting the existing thread-session rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct-target guard now uses the full session thread parser, so loaded/plugin-owned session conversation metadata is considered before dispatch. This keeps Telegram topic handling at the channel/plugin session-key boundary rather than adding Telegram-specific `:topic:` parsing to the generic core suffix parser.

Related PR #99844 covers the same issue by teaching the generic suffix parser about `:topic:`. This PR instead follows the issue review's requested fix shape: reuse the plugin-owned lightweight session-key resolver path for `sessions_send`.

The CI follow-up commit also defers apply-patch fs-safe root startup until guarded write/remove/mkdirp operations need it. That prevents a path-validation rejection from leaving an orphaned root promise that can later fail as an unhandled `FsSafeError: root dir not found` in the agent test shard.

## User Impact

Telegram topic session targets now receive the same parent-session guidance as other thread child sessions. The tool rejects before queueing or dispatching an agent run, so users avoid accidental nested work in the topic child context.

The CI-only apply-patch follow-up has no user-facing behavior change; it keeps the existing workspace safety checks while removing the unhandled rejection that made the current PR head red.

## Evidence

- Current head proved: `08ba470110aa3dd3e919833df1521edb7ac8677c`.
- Claim proved: `sessions_send` rejects a Telegram topic session target before gateway dispatch when the plugin-owned Telegram session-key resolver classifies `:topic:` as a threaded child conversation.
- ClawSweeper follow-up addressed: the regression test leaves the active plugin registry empty and exercises the lightweight bundled `session-key-api` fallback instead of a loaded Telegram registry hook. It asserts the fallback loader was called and `callGatewayMock` was not called.
- Source path checked:
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` calls `parseSessionThreadInfo(resolvedKey).threadId` before dispatch and returns the existing `sessions_send cannot target a thread session...` error when a child thread/topic is detected.
  - `src/config/sessions/thread-info.ts` delegates `parseSessionThreadInfo(...)` to the plugin-aware session conversation resolver, while the fast loaded-only helper remains separate.
  - `src/channels/plugins/session-conversation.ts` prefers loaded plugin hooks, then the activated bundled `session-key-api` public surface, then generic parsing.
  - `extensions/telegram/session-key-api.ts` exports Telegram's owner-owned `resolveSessionConversation` public surface, which resolves `:topic:` ids to `threadId` metadata.
  - `src/agents/apply-patch.ts` now starts the fs-safe root lazily from write/remove/mkdirp operations instead of creating the root promise before path validation.
- Redacted terminal runtime proof from the same PR diff before the merge-main refresh, using a temporary config that enables Telegram, an empty active plugin registry, the real `extensions/telegram/session-key-api.ts` fallback surface, and a counted gateway caller:

```text
node --import tsx .tmp-sessions-send-openclaw-tools-proof.mts
{
  "source": "createSessionsSendTool with real Telegram session-key-api fallback",
  "toolRegistered": true,
  "status": "error",
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:telegram:group:-100123:topic:77",
  "error": "sessions_send cannot target a thread session for inter-agent coordination. Use the parent channel session key instead.",
  "gatewayCalls": 0
}
```

- Current-head focused `sessions_send` regression run:

```text
OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "rejects Telegram topic session targets"

PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects Telegram topic session targets before dispatching an agent run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)
```

- File-level `sessions_send` regression run before the merge-main refresh:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose

PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects direct thread session targets before dispatching an agent run
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects Telegram topic session targets before dispatching an agent run
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects label targets that resolve to canonical thread sessions
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > does not disclose a resolved thread session key from a sessionId target
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  44 passed (44)
```

- CI red-light follow-up: `checks-node-compact-large-2` failed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28702287629/job/85122209850 because the shard passed its test files (`67 passed`, `1276 passed`) and then Vitest reported an unhandled `FsSafeError: root dir not found` from `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts` / `rejects hardlink alias escapes by default`.
- Focused CI-red-light repro proof on current head:

```text
OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "rejects hardlink alias escapes by default"

PASS |agents-core| src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts > applyPatch > rejects hardlink alias escapes by default
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 24 skipped (25)
```

- Focused apply-patch file proof on current head:

```text
OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts --reporter=verbose

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  23 passed | 2 skipped (25)
```

- Hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD` passed after the CI fix; `gh pr diff --name-only` now shows `src/agents/apply-patch.ts`, `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts`.
- CI proof:
  - `check-test-types` passed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28702287629/job/85122209761, which clears the earlier stale `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.dm-threads.test.ts` `mentionSource` type failure from the pre-merge head.
  - Latest pre-fix `Real behavior proof` passed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28702433626/job/85122555207. Current-head CI is rerunning after commit `08ba470110aa3dd3e919833df1521edb7ac8677c`.
- Review: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` reported `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported` after the apply-patch CI fix.
- Not tested / proof gaps: no live Telegram bot/device send was run. The proof is scoped to the changed `sessions_send` runtime boundary: Telegram topic keys are resolved as threaded by the plugin-owned session conversation resolver and are rejected before any gateway dispatch.
